day_title: Day 14: Git collaboration in a disposable repository
day_subtitle: Use branches, diffs, conflicts, safe recovery, and PR-style review without touching the curriculum worktree.
time_budget_label: 480 active minutes (breaks and unattended runtime excluded)

day-14-act-01.title: Branches, diffs, and review
day-14-act-01.prerequisites: Day 13 project artifacts and basic Git status/log/diff.
day-14-act-01.objective: Create a disposable clone, make a focused branch change to the text project, and review the diff before committing.
day-14-act-01.instructions: Required work: build the private base + clone exactly as the reference answer shows (copy ONLY projects/text_tools/{__init__.py,core.py,cli.py} into a new private base — never clone, publish, or mutate the learning repository or its .git, database, .venv, or secrets), then create branch `parser-help`, make the specified one-line --input help improvement, and record branch, status, log, staged + unstaged diffs, and `git diff --check` before a single focused commit. Prove behavior with the public --help check — a diff plus exit code 0 is evidence, not proof. Each block runs inside `( ... )` with `set -e`: it validates the fresh WORKDIR before any use and aborts inside the subshell on a failed mkdir/cp/cd, so a failed command can never fall through and run Git in your current repository - and exports stay out of your caller shell. `d14env` wraps external commands in `env -i`, dropping ambient GIT_DIR/GIT_WORK_TREE/index/object/alternates, GIT_CONFIG*, XDG, template, hook, and signing variables so they cannot steer THESE authored commands; env -i alone does not stop a command from writing outside WORKDIR - the validated preconditions and fail-stop are what keep the authored commands inside it. PATH only selects which executables run (resolved paths are printed; Python is pinned to the absolute PYTHON_BIN) - it is not a trusted-tool list or a filesystem boundary. Environment hygiene, NOT an OS sandbox. Export the printed WORKDIR value yourself - later activity blocks require it. Optional work: a real agent may review your diff against the written plan; if the selected tool is unavailable, record that portion blocked/unexecuted and never fabricate a transcript.
day-14-act-01.exercise_prompt:
Predict exactly which line of `projects/text_tools/cli.py` changes for the --input help improvement and which of the three copied files must remain byte-identical (verify with sha256sum). Explain why `git diff` plus a zero exit code is evidence, not proof, of behavior — and why running through `d14env` (`env -i` + private HOME/XDG/config/template + signing off) matters when GIT_DIR could point at a different repository - and why `( set -e` fail-stop plus the WORKDIR validation keeps a failed cd from ever running Git in the caller's repository. Run this complete private setup and check:

```sh
(
set -e
WORKDIR=$(mktemp -d)
[ -n "$WORKDIR" ] && [ -d "$WORKDIR" ] && [ -w "$WORKDIR" ] && [ -x "$WORKDIR" ] || {
  echo "abort: WORKDIR '$WORKDIR' is missing or unusable - refusing to run anything outside it" >&2
  exit 1
}
LEARN=/absolute/path/to/your/clone
[ -f "$LEARN/projects/text_tools/cli.py" ] || {
  echo "abort: LEARN must point at a checkout containing projects/text_tools/cli.py" >&2
  exit 1
}
export WORKDIR LEARN
mkdir -p "$WORKDIR/home" "$WORKDIR/xdg" "$WORKDIR/tpl" "$WORKDIR/tmp"
d14env() {
  env -i PATH="$PATH" HOME="$WORKDIR/home" XDG_CONFIG_HOME="$WORKDIR/xdg" \
      TMPDIR="$WORKDIR/tmp" WORKDIR="$WORKDIR" LEARN="$LEARN" \
      GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1 GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null \
      GIT_TEMPLATE_DIR="$WORKDIR/tpl" \
      GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=1 GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0=commit.gpgsign GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0=false \
      LC_ALL=C PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 "$@"
}
command -v git sed python3
PYTHON_BIN="$(command -v python3)"
mkdir -p "$WORKDIR/base/projects/text_tools"
cp "$LEARN"/projects/text_tools/__init__.py "$LEARN"/projects/text_tools/core.py "$LEARN"/projects/text_tools/cli.py "$WORKDIR/base/projects/text_tools/"
cd "$WORKDIR/base"
d14env git init
d14env git config user.name "Learner"
d14env git config user.email "learner@example.invalid"
d14env sha256sum projects/text_tools/*.py
d14env git add projects/
d14env git commit -m "text_tools snapshot"
d14env git clone "$WORKDIR/base" "$WORKDIR/clone"
cd "$WORKDIR/clone"
d14env git config user.name "Learner"
d14env git config user.email "learner@example.invalid"
d14env git switch -c parser-help
d14env sed -i 's|corpus file\.|corpus file (UTF-8 by default; override with --encoding/--errors).|' projects/text_tools/cli.py
d14env git status --short
d14env git diff
d14env git diff --cached
d14env git diff --check
d14env git add projects/text_tools/cli.py
d14env git commit -m "cli: document --input decoding defaults"
d14env git log --oneline -3
d14env "$PYTHON_BIN" projects/text_tools/cli.py --help | grep -F "UTF-8 by default"
printf 'export WORKDIR=%s  # run this before the later activity blocks\n' "$WORKDIR"
)
```
day-14-act-01.hint: A `git worktree` is not an independent clone: it shares the base repository's refs and writes `.git/worktrees` metadata (verified). Clone the private base instead. Ambient GIT_DIR/GIT_WORK_TREE/GIT_CONFIG*/XDG variables can redirect git at a different repository or config — `env -i` drops them; it does NOT sandbox the filesystem. Never run reset --hard, clean, force-push, or recovery commands against the learning repository.
day-14-act-01.answer:
Verified observations (Linux, bash, git 2.56; your hashes/timestamps differ):
- `sha256sum` prints three hashes — the base identity; `core.py` and `__init__.py` stay byte-identical throughout.
- `git status --short` shows only ` M projects/text_tools/cli.py`; `git diff` shows the single --input help line; `git diff --cached` is empty until `git add`.
- `git log --oneline` shows the focused commit on top of `text_tools snapshot`.
- The behavioral check: `--help` prints `Path to the input text corpus file (UTF-8 by default; ...` — public evidence the change took effect; the diff alone would only show text moved.
Boundaries: a `git worktree` shares the base's refs and mutates `.git/worktrees` — not an independent clone. Ambient Git environment variables were demonstrated hostile: with GIT_DIR/GIT_WORK_TREE aimed at an unrelated private repository plus a trap global config (foreign user.name, malicious template hooks), this exact block still configured only the private base/clone — the unrelated repository's HEAD and user.name were unchanged, no sentinel hook ran, and commits show `Learner`, not the trap identity. `env -i` keeps only the listed variables; PATH merely locates tools and grants no repository access — this is hygiene, not a filesystem sandbox. `__pycache__/` may appear after running cli.py — untracked build output (PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 prevents it). Linux/bash scope; sed -i is GNU-style — macOS needs `sed -i ''`, Windows differs (reference only, unexecuted).
day-14-act-01.mastery_criterion: Learner can explain branch, commit, diff, and review boundaries with command output attached — including the public --help check demonstrating the new help text — and states that optional agent review was executed, or honestly recorded as blocked/unexecuted.
day-14-act-01.assistance_policy_label: Agent assistance is optional and follows a written plan; the learner owns permissions and verifies every diff and command result. If the selected agent is unavailable, the assisted portion is recorded blocked/unexecuted — never simulated.

day-14-act-02.title: Independent conflict resolution
day-14-act-02.prerequisites: A disposable repository with two divergent branches.
day-14-act-02.objective: Resolve a real text_tools fixture conflict independently and preserve both intended changes.
day-14-act-02.instructions: Required work: FIRST attempt a fresh independent variant — pick a different real cli.py line (for example the --seed help text) and two compatible requirement terms of your own, create the two divergent branches, merge, resolve preserving BOTH terms, and verify each term via a separate --help check plus `git rev-list --parents -n 1 HEAD` (three ids = a merge with two parents). Then compare with the worked reference below, which uses the description line and the terms `Unicode-aware` and `original-byte`. The block reuses the WORKDIR fixture exported by the setup block (or set WORKDIR to that printed path first) and re-declares `d14env`. Official Git documentation may be consulted; no AI output or copied resolution counts as independent mastery. Optional work: compare a reference explanation afterward.
day-14-act-02.exercise_prompt:
Before merging, predict the conflict markers and the final description/line content for your own variant. Explain why blindly choosing ours or theirs loses a requirement, and how a resolution satisfies both acceptance terms. Worked reference sequence (same private clone):

```sh
(
set -e
: "${WORKDIR:?set WORKDIR to the private Day 14 fixture path first}"
[ -d "$WORKDIR/clone/.git" ] || { echo "private clone not found - run the setup block first"; exit 1; }
d14env() {
  env -i PATH="$PATH" HOME="$WORKDIR/home" XDG_CONFIG_HOME="$WORKDIR/xdg" \
      TMPDIR="$WORKDIR/tmp" WORKDIR="$WORKDIR" LEARN="$LEARN" \
      GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1 GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null \
      GIT_TEMPLATE_DIR="$WORKDIR/tpl" \
      GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=1 GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0=commit.gpgsign GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0=false \
      LC_ALL=C PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 "$@"
}
command -v git sed python3
PYTHON_BIN="$(command -v python3)"
cd "$WORKDIR/clone"
d14env git switch -c desc-unicode
d14env sed -i 's|compute statistics, deterministic splits, and provenance artifacts\.|compute Unicode-aware statistics, deterministic splits, and provenance artifacts.|' projects/text_tools/cli.py
d14env git commit -am "describe Unicode-aware statistics"
d14env git switch -
d14env git switch -c desc-provenance
d14env sed -i 's|and provenance artifacts\.|and original-byte provenance artifacts.|' projects/text_tools/cli.py
d14env git commit -am "describe original-byte provenance"
if d14env git merge desc-unicode; then
  echo "unexpected: merge resolved cleanly" >&2
  exit 1
else
  echo "expected non-zero exit (content conflict): $?"
fi
d14env sed -n '/<<<<<<</,/>>>>>>>/p' projects/text_tools/cli.py
d14env "$PYTHON_BIN" - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
p = Path('projects/text_tools/cli.py')
s = p.read_text()
i = s.index('<<<<<<<')
j = s.index('\n', s.index('>>>>>>>', i))
resolved = '        description="Text and Data Tools: compute Unicode-aware statistics, deterministic splits, and original-byte provenance artifacts."\n'
p.write_text(s[:i] + resolved + s[j+1:])
PY
d14env git add projects/text_tools/cli.py
d14env git commit -m "merge: keep both requirements"
d14env git rev-list --parents -n 1 HEAD
d14env "$PYTHON_BIN" projects/text_tools/cli.py --help | grep -F "Unicode-aware"
d14env "$PYTHON_BIN" projects/text_tools/cli.py --help | grep -F "original-byte"
d14env git status --short
)
```
day-14-act-02.hint: Read every marker line (`<<<<<<<`, `=======`, `>>>>>>>`), restate both acceptance terms before editing, edit only the conflicted region, then run `git diff --check`, two separate --help checks, and `git rev-list --parents -n 1 HEAD`.
day-14-act-02.answer:
Verified observations:
- `git merge desc-unicode` exits non-zero with `CONFLICT (content)` in cli.py; the file contains the marker block with HEAD's `original-byte provenance` line versus desc-unicode's `Unicode-aware` line.
- The worked resolution keeps both: `compute Unicode-aware statistics, deterministic splits, and original-byte provenance artifacts.`
- `git rev-list --parents -n 1 HEAD` prints three ids — the merge has two parents.
- Both `--help | grep -F` checks succeed; `git status --short` is clean; `git diff --check` is clean.
The assessed attempt is the learner's own variant (different line, own terms); this worked case is the reference. `ours`/`theirs` alone keeps only one requirement. Your completed variant stays on its own branches — later reference continuations rebuild their own baseline and never discard it.
day-14-act-02.mastery_criterion: Unaided resolution on the learner's own variant is correct: both requirement terms verified via --help, the merge commit with two parents recorded, and the evidence names the conflict, chosen behavior, checks, and safe boundary.
day-14-act-02.assistance_policy_label: Independent Mastery Check: no AI or copied conflict resolution; official Git documentation may be consulted.

day-14-act-03.title: Safe recovery
day-14-act-03.prerequisites: A committed disposable fixture and a deliberate, reversible mistake.
day-14-act-03.objective: Recover from an accidental edit or unwanted commit using safe, non-destructive operations.
day-14-act-03.instructions: Required work in the same private clone: (0) establish the CANONICAL reference baseline — branch `d14-ref` from `parser-help` and commit the resolved description line; your sealed independent attempt stays on its own branches and is never discarded. (A) back up cli.py, reproduce the two-hunk unstaged case (MISTAKE typo on the description line + KEEP edit on the --seed help line), inspect `git diff`, undo ONLY the typo, verify the KEEP hunk survives, then COMMIT the valid edit — a committed change cannot be dropped by the later cleanup demos. (B) staged-vs-worktree on a fresh single-hunk mistake: stage it, show `git restore <path>` leaves it in the index, then `--staged` plus a whole-path discard — now justified because the only remaining change is genuinely unwanted; verify the tree is clean AND the committed KEEP still works via --help. (C) commit a known single-parent BAD change followed by an independent GOOD change, revert BAD with a new commit, and prove GOOD and KEEP survive and history was not rewritten; finally observe (expected failure) that reverting a merge demands an -m mainline choice. Optional work: review the recovery choices with an agent after the run.
day-14-act-03.exercise_prompt:
For an unstaged typo sharing a file with a valid edit, and separately for a bad single-parent commit followed by a good commit: choose between `git restore`, `git revert`, and the saved copy — and predict the resulting diff and history before running. Why must the KEEP edit be committed BEFORE the staged-mistake demo rather than merely survive it in the worktree?

```sh
(
set -e
: "${WORKDIR:?set WORKDIR to the private Day 14 fixture path first}"
[ -d "$WORKDIR/clone/.git" ] || { echo "private clone not found - run the setup block first"; exit 1; }
d14env() {
  env -i PATH="$PATH" HOME="$WORKDIR/home" XDG_CONFIG_HOME="$WORKDIR/xdg" \
      TMPDIR="$WORKDIR/tmp" WORKDIR="$WORKDIR" LEARN="$LEARN" \
      GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1 GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null \
      GIT_TEMPLATE_DIR="$WORKDIR/tpl" \
      GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=1 GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0=commit.gpgsign GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0=false \
      LC_ALL=C PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 "$@"
}
command -v git sed python3
PYTHON_BIN="$(command -v python3)"
cd "$WORKDIR/clone"
d14env git switch -c d14-ref parser-help
d14env sed -i 's|compute statistics, deterministic splits, and provenance artifacts\.|compute Unicode-aware statistics, deterministic splits, and original-byte provenance artifacts.|' projects/text_tools/cli.py
d14env git commit -am "reference baseline: description keeps both requirement terms"
d14env sed -i 's|Unicode-aware statistics|statistisc|' projects/text_tools/cli.py
d14env sed -i 's|(default: 42)\.|(default: 42; any integer).|' projects/text_tools/cli.py
d14env cp projects/text_tools/cli.py "$WORKDIR/cli-backup.py"
d14env git diff
d14env sed -i 's|statistisc|Unicode-aware statistics|' projects/text_tools/cli.py
d14env git diff
d14env git diff --check
d14env "$PYTHON_BIN" projects/text_tools/cli.py --help | grep -F "any integer"
d14env git commit -am "document that --seed accepts any integer"
d14env sed -i 's|default=42,|default=7,|' projects/text_tools/cli.py
d14env git add projects/text_tools/cli.py
d14env git status --short
d14env git restore projects/text_tools/cli.py
d14env bash -c 'git diff --cached | grep -F "default=7"'
d14env git restore --staged projects/text_tools/cli.py
d14env git restore projects/text_tools/cli.py
d14env git status --short
d14env bash -c 'test -z "$(git status --porcelain)"'
d14env "$PYTHON_BIN" projects/text_tools/cli.py --help | grep -F "any integer"
d14env sed -i 's|default=42,|default=7,|' projects/text_tools/cli.py
d14env git commit -am "BAD: change default seed to 7"
BAD=$(d14env git rev-parse HEAD)
d14env sed -i 's|(default: 0.1)\.|(default: 0.1; must be in [0, 1]).|' projects/text_tools/cli.py
d14env git commit -am "GOOD: clarify split-ratio range"
d14env git revert --no-edit "$BAD"
d14env grep -F "default=42," projects/text_tools/cli.py
d14env grep -F "must be in [0, 1]" projects/text_tools/cli.py
d14env grep -F "any integer" projects/text_tools/cli.py
d14env git log --oneline -3
d14env git rev-list --count HEAD
MERGE_SHA=$(d14env git rev-list --all --merges -n 1)
[ -n "$MERGE_SHA" ] || { echo "no merge commit found - run the act-02 reference merge first" >&2; exit 1; }
if d14env git revert "$MERGE_SHA" 2>"$WORKDIR/merge_revert.err"; then
  echo "unexpected: merge revert succeeded without -m" >&2
  exit 1
else
  rc=$?
  grep -F "no -m option" "$WORKDIR/merge_revert.err" && echo "expected non-zero exit (merge needs -m): $rc"
fi
)
```
day-14-act-03.hint: `git restore <path>` defaults to restoring the worktree FROM the index and discards EVERY unstaged hunk in that path — and after `--staged` un-stages mixed content, a whole-path restore discards ALL of it, including previously rescued edits that were never committed. Preserve valid work by committing it before any destructive demo. `git revert` adds a new commit and needs `-m` for merges. Never reset --hard, clean, or force-push.
day-14-act-03.answer:
Verified observations:
- Baseline: `d14-ref` created from `parser-help` with the resolved description committed — independent variant branches stay untouched.
- After the two edits, `git diff` shows two hunks (distant lines); whole-path restore would discard both — the unrelated KEEP edit too (independently reproduced counterexample). After the targeted undo, `git diff` shows only the KEEP hunk and --help prints `any integer`; the KEEP commit `document that --seed accepts any integer` then protects it.
- Staged mistake: after `git restore <path>`, `git diff --cached` still shows `default=7` — the default source is the index; `--staged` un-stages it, and whole-path discard is now correct because the only remaining change is unwanted. Post-cleanup checkpoint: `git status --porcelain` is EMPTY and --help still prints `any integer` — the KEEP survived because it was committed, not merely uncommitted-rescued.
- Single-parent revert: `git revert --no-edit $BAD` creates a new commit; `default=42` restored, `must be in [0, 1]` (GOOD) and `any integer` (KEEP) both present; `git log --oneline` shows Revert, GOOD, BAD — nothing rewritten; `git rev-list --count HEAD` grows.
- Expected failure: `git revert <merge-sha>` exits 128 with `is a merge but no -m option was given` — a merge has two parents; choosing the mainline is a decision, not a default. `git rev-list --all --merges -n 1` locates a merge across your branches; if you never merged, run the act-02 reference merge first.
Shared history is simulated locally; nothing pushed or published. Backup at $WORKDIR/cli-backup.py preserved pre-recovery bytes.
day-14-act-03.mastery_criterion: Learner establishes the canonical baseline without discarding sealed work, justifies each operation from repository state, proves the KEEP edit survives AFTER cleanup via its own commit and a clean status plus --help check, shows the revert created a new commit without rewriting history, and observed the merge-revert failure without guessing a mainline.
day-14-act-03.assistance_policy_label: Agent-assisted engineering check: the agent may explain options, but the learner executes and verifies every step; an unavailable tool is recorded blocked/unexecuted.

day-14-act-04.title: PR-style review and retrieval
day-14-act-04.prerequisites: Completed branch, conflict, and recovery evidence.
day-14-act-04.objective: Review a disposable change as if it were a pull request, separating correctness, scope, tests, risks, and evidence.
day-14-act-04.instructions: Required work: FIRST record your prediction/initial hypothesis unaided; then run the weak and strong checks yourself in the same private WORKDIR fixture — your own execution is part of the unaided attempt, not assistance; then write and seal (submit, date) the completed UNAIDED review — acceptance criteria, blocking findings, non-blocking findings, the actual observed evidence, and boundaries. If the behavior turns out correct, the sealed review still records the checks run and why they suffice — a bare 'looks fine' fails. Optional work: afterward compare a real agent review labeled assisted (never a replacement for the sealed draft); any assisted correction requires a fresh unaided recheck. External publication is not authorized.
day-14-act-04.exercise_prompt:
Before running the strong check, predict whether `--help` listing `--quiet` proves the flag works. Name the defect the weak smoke check cannot see and the stronger CLI check that exposes it. The patch (reviewer-authored, not observed agent output):

```sh
(
set -e
: "${WORKDIR:?set WORKDIR to your private Day 14 fixture path first}"
[ -d "$WORKDIR/clone/.git" ] || { echo "private clone not found - run the setup block first"; exit 1; }
d14env() {
  env -i PATH="$PATH" HOME="$WORKDIR/home" XDG_CONFIG_HOME="$WORKDIR/xdg" \
      TMPDIR="$WORKDIR/tmp" WORKDIR="$WORKDIR" LEARN="$LEARN" \
      GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1 GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null \
      GIT_TEMPLATE_DIR="$WORKDIR/tpl" \
      GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=1 GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0=commit.gpgsign GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0=false \
      LC_ALL=C PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 "$@"
}
command -v git sed python3
PYTHON_BIN="$(command -v python3)"
cd "$WORKDIR/clone"
d14env git switch -c add-quiet
d14env "$PYTHON_BIN" - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
p = Path('projects/text_tools/cli.py')
s = p.read_text()
old = '    parser.add_argument(\n        "--errors",'
assert s.count(old) == 1
s = s.replace(old, '''    parser.add_argument(
        "--quiet",
        action="store_true",
        help="Suppress the artifact-generation success summary.",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--errors",''')
p.write_text(s)
PY
d14env git commit -am "add --quiet flag"
d14env "$PYTHON_BIN" projects/text_tools/cli.py --help | grep -F -- "--quiet"
mkdir -p "$WORKDIR/acts"
d14env printf 'a\nb\nc\n' > "$WORKDIR/acts/in.txt"
d14env "$PYTHON_BIN" projects/text_tools/cli.py --input "$WORKDIR/acts/in.txt" --split --output-dir "$WORKDIR/acts/out" --quiet
)
```
day-14-act-04.hint: Review behavior at the CLI seam — public flags and stdout — not private internals. A check that only inspects --help passes even when the required behavior is absent.
day-14-act-04.answer:
Verified observations:
- Weak check passes: `--help` lists `--quiet  Suppress the artifact-generation success summary.`
- Strong check fails the requirement: `--quiet --split` stdout still contains `Data artifacts generated successfully` — the flag is parsed but never read.
- Chronology: prediction recorded first, own checks executed unaided, then the report sealed — never sealed before the evidence exists and never silently rewritten afterward.
Worked review report (sealed, unaided):
- Blocking: --quiet accepted but never used; required behavior absent -> reject this patch.
- Non-blocking: help text could name which output lines are suppressed.
- Evidence: the --help output line and the observed --quiet stdout quoted above.
- Boundaries: the patch is reviewer-authored (illustrative), not real agent output; my checks are public CLI runs I executed inside the private fixture, not a hidden platform evaluator; nothing was published or pushed.
- No-defect alternative: if --quiet actually suppressed the summary, the report records the same checks plus 'no defect found' and why — never 'looks fine' alone.
day-14-act-04.mastery_criterion: The sealed unaided review states the acceptance criterion (summary suppressed under --quiet), cites stdout actually observed in the learner's own runs, separates blocking from non-blocking findings, distinguishes the hypothetical patch from real agent output and own checks from a hidden evaluator, and was sealed after the recorded prediction and own checks, before any assisted comparison.
day-14-act-04.assistance_policy_label: Independent Mastery Check: prediction, own checks, and the sealed review are all unaided; the later assisted comparison is separate and never replaces it.
